title: Lost in Atlantic City, gambling with Charlie Johnson
summary: Out of school and adrift, he gambles with Johnson, whom he calls a great cabaret pianist and bandleader who died poor.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Okay, so you're talking about Atlantic City after the summer's over in September. At this point were you staying in Atlantic City in the winter time, too? Were you living there?

Well, no. I'm trying to live there. 'Cause see, I don't want to go back to school, and I don't want to go back to Philadelphia where my people are and all, you see. I'm lost. I don't know what to do. That's right, I'm really lost. I don't know what it's all about. I jumped out of school and followed this girl, you know what I mean. And I got down there, and it was like that song said, 'After you get what you want, you don't want it.' Now I've got it and I run into Charlie Johnson and I think he's the greatest, you know what I mean, and he's struggling to get better and he turned out to be one of the greatest cabaret pianists and band leaders that we had. But, he died very poor because he would do one thing, he'd gamble. He and I -- I used to gamble with him, you know. I used to stay out all night to get this money and I'd wait, and then on Saturday night when I got the job, working, we'd go to a gambling joint.
